About these prices & taxes

How this works: coverage is every country where Apple runs an official online store — 40 countries — plus all 50 US states and DC and all 13 Canadian provinces & territories, 102 regions in total, because North American tax is set state by state, not nationally. Countries in grey have no Apple online store, so Apple publishes no official price there. US & Canada list prices exclude tax, so tax is added at each state’s or province’s own rate: in the US that runs from 0% in Oregon, Delaware, Montana and New Hampshire up to a ~10.11% combined state-and-local average in Louisiana (California ~9.04%, Florida ~7.02%, Texas ~8.20% — US figures are the combined state + average local sales tax, Tax Foundation 2025); in Canada it runs from 5% GST-only in Alberta, Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut, through Ontario’s 13% HST and Quebec’s 14.975% GST+QST, up to 15% HST in New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland & Labrador (Nova Scotia 14% HST). That is exactly why Alberta is cheaper than Ontario for the same product: same Canadian list price, 8 points less tax. Everywhere else Apple’s store price already includes VAT/GST and is converted to the display currency. The tax breakdown shown with each price splits it the same way it is charged: in the US the before-tax figure is the US list price and tax is added at that state’s rate; in Canada the Canadian list price is split back out at that province’s GST/PST/HST rate; everywhere else the after-tax total is split back out at the standard VAT/GST rate named in the breakdown (Hong Kong has no sales tax or VAT, so its before-tax and after-tax prices are the same). Brazil is the one exception: several federal and state taxes are baked into its store price with no single rate, so only its after-tax total is shown, with no invented split. Every price shown on this globe is that product’s own real price, read live from that country’s own official Apple Store on 15 Nov 2026 — no price is a modelled estimate, an anchor or a ratio any more. For the whole current iPhone line-up (iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, Duo, Air, 17, 17e and, where it is still sold, iPhone 16), the base-configuration price in every store country is Apple’s exact live list price in local currency, read from that store’s own buy pages — so the globe’s colours and the ranking for the default view are live store prices end to end. Store audit — online & physical stores by country (checked 15 Nov 2026)

Every country priced on this globe was checked on 15 Nov 2026 against apple.com, samsung.com and the brands’ own store lists. “Online” means an official online store you can actually check out on; “Store” means a physical brand store (an Apple Store, or a Samsung Experience Store / Samsung brand store) — authorised resellers do not count. A country with no official online store shows no price for that brand: it stays grey on the globe. A country with an online store but no physical store keeps its price and is marked “Online only” in the panel and the ranking above.

Samsung does not publish who runs each Experience Store, and many outside South Korea and the US are partner-run — “Yes” means a Samsung-branded store exists there, not that Samsung operates it directly. Switzerland’s Samsung store entry rests on a Samsung in-store presence at Sihlcity, Zurich; China’s could not be confirmed either way after 2026 outlet closures, and no Irish Samsung Experience Store could be found.

One reverse case exists worldwide: Macao has physical Apple Stores but no Apple online store, so it has no price of its own here. “—” means that brand’s stores were not part of this audit for that country, because the country is not priced in that brand’s mode.
